topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: Lord have mercy, the tree I planted, the one I grew up with, it's gone. Just vanished, as if a great hand swept it away. All those years, through the cold and the clammy, the droughts and the downpours, it stood there, sturdy as a sentry. Now, a stump marks the spot, cold and stark. The orchard’s guardian, my little sapling turned giant, turned into firewood or logs for a stranger's hearth. Each ring inside told a story, tales of springs I danced around it, summers spent in its shade. I can't fathom who'd do such a thing, but the field whispers it's no longer my business to ask. My hands ache, not from toil but from what I can't touch anymore.
